source.title: Gradient Descent Converges Linearly to Flatter Minima than Gradient Flow in Shallow Linear Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied, including appendices; some equations and symbols are garbled by text extraction, but the study is identifiable and its main claims and results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes gradient descent training behavior and convergence in a depth-2 linear network using a theoretical model and analysis, rather than testing the benchmark CNN recipes named in the versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports theoretical convergence, imbalance, and sharpness results for a depth-2 linear network trained on a scalar squared-loss objective. Its CIFAR, random-label, shortcut, initialization, batch-normalization, and two-layer ReLU teacher-student recipes are not tested. Figure 3 is described qualitatively, without extractable numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study's own analysis bears on V5: exact gradient descent on a depth-2 linear squared-loss network can converge with step sizes above 2/λ, sometimes very slowly. This is a theoretical test of convergence beyond a stability threshold; it does not establish the full catapult trajectory or sustained sharpness hovering.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate. Under specified step-size and initialization conditions, gradient descent converges linearly to a global minimum in the depth-2 linear squared-loss model; larger permitted steps can still converge much more slowly. Discrete updates reduce imbalance and final norm/sharpness relative to gradient flow, revealing a speed–regularization trade-off. Extensions to deeper, nonlinear, vector-input, and stochastic training remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical analysis of exact gradient descent on a depth-2 linear network with a single scalar input and output, parameterized by a dot product, under squared loss; the paper identifies vector-valued inputs, deeper models, nonlinear activations, and SGD as future extensions.
record.method_sensitivity: Step size affects convergence rate and final parameter imbalance/sharpness; initialization region and imbalance affect convergence behavior. Figure 3 qualitatively compares step sizes and initial scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Discrete gradient descent reduces parameter imbalance and selects lower-norm, flatter minima than gradient flow under the stated conditions; stronger regularization is associated with slower convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this depth-2 linear squared-loss model, discretization creates an implicit-regularization versus convergence-speed trade-off.

record.problems: The study is a highly simplified theoretical model, not a benchmark network experiment. It explicitly leaves deeper, nonlinear, vector-input, and stochastic-gradient cases for future work. No uncertainty estimates or empirical controls are reported. Figure 3 has qualitative descriptions but no numerical values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: the study's results are theoretical claims and bounds for a scalar squared-loss depth-2 linear model, not separately reported experimental outcomes with a subject, condition, measure, and value as required for rows. Figure 3 contains qualitative plotted comparisons without recoverable values.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and model-size or regularization comparisons.
Spurious local minima in ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep tanh initialization, and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.

An initial loss rise followed by curvature reduction and recovery relative to the initial linearized model's threshold; sustained sharpness growth and hovering at 2/η; divergence at larger rates or from initially subthreshold sharpness. The paper's discussion of these trajectories in other networks cites prior studies.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: A theoretical result row for convergence beyond the stability threshold, recording the model, step-size conditions, exceptional trajectories, and slow-convergence regime. The record declares theoretical results excluded, but that exclusion leaves its tested V5 result unrepresented.
missing.locator: Section 5, Theorem 2 and Edge-of-Stability Case; Appendix F.1, equations (66)–(68).

record.verdict_notes: The approximately 4/sharpness convergence guarantee discussed in Related Work is attributed to Wang et al. (2022); it should not be presented as this paper's new result. Figure 3 reports qualitative imbalance and convergence-time comparisons, without establishing the full V5 trajectory.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification, convolutional networks, random or corrupted labels, SGD/Adam, model size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, standard initialization, spurious minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, batch normalization, depth effects, ImageNet/CIFAR-10, tanh special initialization, and Fixup.
Activation-matched initializations, signal/gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and deep or convolutional network depth.

Tests the relation between learning rate, stability-related thresholds, convergence speed, and training loss in a depth-2 linear squared-loss network. Does not test wide-network initial linearized thresholds, full-batch neural-network sharpness hovering, or the cited divergence cases. Theoretical results are stated, but no version-specific numeric run values are provided.
Batch normalization speed or learning-rate tolerance, MNIST/CIFAR-10/ImageNet models, and Fixup without normalization.

relationships.condition: Exact gradient descent on the scalar-input/output depth-2 linear squared-loss model, within the stated convergence conditions and excluding exceptional saddle-reaching trajectories.
relationships.reason: Based on text rather than extracted rows: Section 5 and Appendix F.1 establish convergence in specified regimes beyond η = 2/λ, with potentially slow oscillatory decay. This supports V5's above-threshold convergence component; no row IDs are available.
relationships.display_finding: Gradient descent converges in specified regimes beyond η = 2/λ, potentially with slow oscillatory decay.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
